extracted.intended_audience: Recipients (K-12 and postsecondary educational institutions), Title IX Coordinators, school administrators, disability services staff, and institutional legal/compliance advisors
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory guidance on (1) confidentiality and permissible disclosures of supportive measures, including FERPA and federal-award exceptions, (2) requirements for consultation when providing supportive measures to students with disabilities, and (3) standards, procedures, and guardrails for emergency removals of respondents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on disclosures about supportive measures (§106.44(g)(5))
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must prohibit disclosures about supportive measures to persons other than the person to whom they apply; the Department replaced “complainant or respondent” with “the person to whom they apply.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The provision limits disclosure of supportive measures, and the Department incorporated exceptions from §106.44(j)(1)-(5). For clarity, the Department combined prior sentences and deleted wording such as “ensure that it does.”

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of nondisclosure — any information about supportive measures (not just PII)
rubrics_metrics.description: §106.44(g)(5) applies to any information about supportive measures (not limited to personally identifiable information), because the information about the supportive measure itself warrants protection even when identities are known.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: If a complainant receives counseling and the respondent already knows the complainant's identity, the respondent is not entitled to know that the complainant is receiving counseling services. Disclosure is permitted only if an exception in §106.44(j)(1)-(5) applies or disclosure is necessary to restore or preserve access to the education program or activity (e.g., informing one party that another moved dorms to maintain a stay-away order).

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitted exceptions to nondisclosure (incorporation of §106.44(j) exceptions)
rubrics_metrics.description: §106.44(g)(5) permits disclosure if any of the exceptions in §106.44(j)(1) through (5) applies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permitted examples include: prior written consent from the person receiving the supportive measure (§106.44(j)(1)); disclosures to parents of minors in elementary or secondary school (§106.44(j)(2)); disclosures required by Federal laws/regulations or terms of a Federal award (§106.44(j)(4)).

rubrics_metrics.name: FERPA interplay with disclosure of supportive measures
rubrics_metrics.description: FERPA does not categorically preclude disclosure of supportive measures; recipients may disclose PII from education records to other school officials with a legitimate educational interest as set forth in the recipient's annual FERPA notification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even where FERPA permits disclosure to school officials, §106.44(g)(5) limits informing one party of supportive measures provided to another unless necessary to restore or preserve access. Recipients should consult the FERPA rules (34 CFR 99.7(a)(3)(iii), 99.31(a)(1)(i)(A)) and include criteria for 'legitimate educational interest' in annual notifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protection applies beyond complainants/respondents
rubrics_metrics.description: The nondisclosure rule was broadened to ensure supportive measures provided to a person who does not make a complaint are encompassed — hence use of “the person to whom they apply.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Nothing in this provision derogates legal rights of a parent, guardian, or authorized representative to act on behalf of a complainant, respondent, or other person.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title IX Coordinator consultation for students with disabilities (§106.44(g)(6)(i))
rubrics_metrics.description: When providing supportive measures for elementary or secondary students with disabilities, the recipient must require the Title IX Coordinator to consult with one or more members, as appropriate, of the student's IEP team or Section 504 team.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department clarified the Title IX Coordinator need not consult the entire IEP/Section 504 team or mandate IEP/504 meetings; consultation must occur with at least one member and is the recipient's duty to ensure. The term 'Section 504 team' was removed from the regulatory text because it does not appear in Section 504 regulations, but consultation with appropriate disability personnel remains required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose and limits of consultation with IEP/Section 504 teams
rubrics_metrics.description: The consultation is for purposes of complying with Title IX and to determine how supportive measures intersect with obligations under IDEA and Section 504; mere consultation does not ensure compliance with IDEA/Section 504 because those statutes operate independently.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consultation may identify additional measures necessary to ensure compliance with IDEA/Section 504. Recipients may convene fuller IEP/504 meetings or consult broadly if appropriate, but the regulation does not prescribe specific decisionmaking processes or particular individuals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Access to disability-related education records in connection with supportive measures
rubrics_metrics.description: A Title IX Coordinator's access to education records (IEP, Section 504 plan) in the course of implementing supportive measures may constitute a legitimate educational interest under FERPA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients should define 'legitimate educational interest' in their annual FERPA notification (34 CFR 99.7(a)(3)(iii)) and treat access solely in connection with implementation of supportive measures consistent with FERPA (34 CFR 99.31(a)(1)(i)(A)).

rubrics_metrics.name: No mandated additional publication re: Title IX Coordinator availability
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department declined to require a postsecondary institution's disability services office to publish a separate notice about Title IX Coordinator availability for students with disabilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The notice of nondiscrimination required by §106.8(c)(1) is considered sufficient to notify community members about Title IX obligations, though recipients may provide additional notice voluntarily if appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emergency removal standard — 'imminent and serious threat' (§106.44(h))
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients may remove a respondent on an emergency basis when the respondent poses an imminent and serious threat to the health or safety of a complainant, or any students, employees, or other persons arising from allegations of sex discrimination; the Department replaced 'immediate' with 'imminent.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The standard encompasses serious non-physical threats (e.g., stalking) as well as physical threats. Emergency removal is intended for imminent/serious threats and is not a substitute for grievance procedures addressing sex discrimination generally.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required procedural guardrails for emergency removal
rubrics_metrics.description: Before or after emergency removal, recipients must: (1) undertake an individualized safety and risk analysis; (2) determine that an imminent and serious threat to health or safety arising from allegations of sex discrimination justifies removal; and (3) provide the respondent with notice and an opportunity to challenge the decision immediately following the removal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department declined to prescribe detailed post-removal procedures or a maximum time limit; the essential due process protections required are notice and an opportunity to be heard immediately following removal. Recipients retain discretion over exact procedures for post-removal challenges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emergency removal need not follow full grievance procedures first
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients are not required to follow the grievance procedures in §106.45 (or §106.46, if applicable) before effectuating an emergency removal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department declined to require pre-removal grievance proceedings because emergency situations may require immediate action; however, if permanent removal or expulsion is sought, the recipient must use established grievance procedures before taking such permanent action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Partial emergency removals and supportive measures that burden respondents
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients may, in appropriate circumstances, remove a respondent only from part of the recipient's education program or activity (e.g., certain classes, teams, clubs) rather than the entire program; supportive measures that burden a respondent (including limited removals) are distinct from full emergency removals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The 2020 amendments and these final regulations permit narrowing removal to reduce burden on respondents when sufficient to address safety risk. Commenters suggested providing alternative access to academic/work responsibilities; recipients have discretion to mitigate burdens. Whether the procedures for emergency removal apply to burdensome supportive measures depends on whether the emergency removal requirements are met.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and assessment flexibility — individualized risk/threat analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department declined to rigidly define 'emergency' or 'serious' and recognizes recipients use different terms; recipients satisfy §106.44(h) by having a process to conduct an analysis of safety and risk particular to the respondent and circumstances, regardless of terminology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The term 'serious' is intentionally flexible to allow individualized assessment. The Department replaced 'immediate' with 'imminent' to distinguish threats requiring immediate law enforcement response versus those appropriate for recipient risk assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protection for expressive conduct / First Amendment considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Emergency removal applies to all forms of sex discrimination, but removal is limited to circumstances that meet the high 'imminent and serious threat' standard; speech that merely articulates a viewpoint is unlikely to meet that standard.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Title IX enforcement under these provisions is to be consistent with First Amendment protections. The Department does not expect offensive or strongly expressed viewpoints alone to justify emergency removal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interaction with IDEA/Section 504 when supportive measures may alter placement
rubrics_metrics.description: Supportive measures that are burdensome and may result in unilateral placement changes under IDEA/Section 504 raise questions about manifestation determination and other IDEA procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commenters asked for clarification that burdensome supportive measures cannot interfere with a respondent's access to special education services or accommodations, and that required IDEA manifestation determination reviews would not violate §106.45(b)(3). The Department reiterates that §106.44(g)(6) does not abrogate obligations under ADA, IDEA, or Section 504.
